problem.text: Lower bounds for homomorphism densities of bipartite graphs (Sidorenko's conjecture) and which bipartite graphs force quasirandomness (the question of Chung, Graham, Wilson and of Skokan and Thoma).

claims.text: Theorem 1.1 and its corollary Theorem 1.2: Sidorenko holds for every bipartite graph with a vertex complete to the other part; Corollary 1.1: t_H >= t_{K2}^{m+w} with w the width; Theorem 1.3: the forcing conjecture holds when two vertices of one part are complete to the other part; Conjecture 2: a graph is forcing if and only if it is bipartite and contains a cycle.

assumptions.text: Finite host graphs and the normalized homomorphism density; the tensor power trick to remove constant factors; the forcing statements use that K_{2,2} and stars satisfy Sidorenko.

methods.text: Dependent random choice (Lemmas 2.1-2.3) to show most small subsets of a random neighbourhood have large common neighbourhoods, then the tensor power trick; forcing via the K_{2,2} density.

limitations.text: The vertex-complete hypothesis excludes most graphs; the general correlation inequality (6) is false (London's path counterexample); the forcing conjecture is left open beyond the stated class.

relevance.text: Positive class used to locate the 2026 counterexample (which has no vertex complete to the other part); source of the forcing conjecture that the 2026 manuscript refutes; Theorem 1.2 is also the base case for the doubling argument this record uses for reflection-symmetric triangulated spheres.
